queries.purpose: Refresh toolchain and PyTorch semantics for the current stack: forced-late block-cache allocation, uninitialized late K/V cache tensors, pinned side-stream H2D metadata migration, CUDA stream synchronization, and CUDA Graph safety.
queries.query: As of July 2026, are there official PyTorch CUDA documentation changes about torch.empty uninitialized allocation, pinned host memory non_blocking H2D copies on CUDA streams, or CUDA Graph safety that would affect using environment-gated late KV cache allocation and side-stream metadata migration?

queries.purpose: Refresh adjacent streaming/block-cache and per-layer KV-cache capacity evidence before selecting bounded lower-capacity schedules on the retained RetroInfer stack.
queries.query: Find recent public implementations or documentation for LLM KV cache block-cache residency, per-layer KV cache capacity reduction, streaming/on-demand GPU KV cache, or host-to-device prefetch overlap relevant to preserving throughput while reducing GPU memory.

sources.title: River861/RetrievalAttention
sources.relevance: The local target repository already exposes environment-gated late block-cache allocation, pinned side-stream late metadata migration, uninitialized late block-cache init, async cluster ID copy, buffer multiplier, and per-layer capacity scaling controls used in this bounded opt014 check.

sources.title: PyTorch CUDA semantics and memory APIs
sources.relevance: CUDA stream and synchronization semantics remain relevant to the pinned side-stream metadata migration path; no material documentation update required a source mechanism pivot for opt014.

sources.title: PyTorch torch.empty
sources.relevance: torch.empty remains an uninitialized allocation primitive, so the retained opt013 uninitialized late block-cache policy stays valid only under the existing write-before-read safety invariant.

sources.title: CAKE: Cascading and Adaptive KV Cache Eviction with Layer Preferences
sources.relevance: Recent per-layer KV-cache allocation evidence supports testing layer-specific capacity schedules, but does not replace the project-native block-cache controls or require a new harness.

sources.title: kvcached virtualized elastic KV cache
sources.relevance: Adjacent streaming/on-demand KV-cache residency work reinforces the objective, but it is a separate serving-system mechanism and not a bounded code pivot for this opt014 schedule check.

sources.title: LMCache
sources.relevance: Tiered KV-cache reuse/offload remains adjacent evidence for streaming residency; opt014 should continue using RetroInfer's existing per-layer block-cache capacity controls rather than importing a new infrastructure stack.

material_updates.action: Reuse the current opt013 stack and bound the search to at most three prior lower-capacity schedules.
material_updates.finding: The fresh frontier search found adjacent per-layer and streaming KV-cache work, but no project-native or toolchain evidence that justifies a new mechanism or harness pivot for this node.
material_updates.impact: Proceed with RETROINFER_LAYER_CACHE_CAPACITY_SCALE schedules on top of late allocation, pinned side-stream metadata migration, uninitialized late block-cache init, async cluster ID copy, and RETROINFER_BUFFER_NPROBE_MULTIPLIER=3.0.

material_updates.finding: PyTorch's uninitialized-memory semantics still require that tensors are fully written before read, and side-stream H2D copies still require explicit synchronization before dependent decode work.
material_updates.impact: Only raw runs with clean exit and RETROINFER_OUTPUT_JSON.all_outputs_contain_groundtruth=true can be compared; no timing claim is made for a schedule that fails this gate.

decision_impact: Bounded opt014 should measure the requested lower-capacity schedules on real A100 hardware and retain a schedule only if it reduces block-cache/peak memory without worse decode or e2e generated throughput versus opt013; otherwise record the capacity frontier as refuted on the current stack.
